analysis.title: View From The Knowledge Network
key_insights: UBS's Rebecca Cheong estimates $75-$100B of risk control selling on Monday 11/2, which could continue Tuesday. After that, selling pressure from systematic funds should fall, setting the stage for a recovery.
Despite the large Nasdaq decline on Friday, excess sell-flow was only $8B for the Nasdaq and -$24B for the SPX.

Late-day excess flow on Friday reversed to +$72B of buying, consistent with aggressive UBS RMM buying from 2:45pm onward. Retail bought the dip, with the most activity in Tech ETFs and Semis/Memory stocks, among Friday's worst-performing segments.

CTA selling was a key driver Friday, with 10 sell triggers across ES1, NQ1 and RTY1. Exposures have fallen to the 19th, 13th and 15th percentile vs 3 years respectively. Only NQ1 retains 3 close sell triggers, while ES1 and RTY1 triggers are farther away and less clustered, suggesting limited additional CTA impact.
Michael Romano: funding fears spiked in October and incremental dollars have found it harder to reach Tech. Capex funding deals are offering attractive yields and drawing capital into credit markets.
Elevated Tech exposures led investors to rotate away from Tech into a broadening-out trade. SPX equal weight outperformed SPX by 6% in October. Hyperscaler EPS did little to slow this trend.

Healthcare is the clear winner of the equity rotation, with XLV +23% in H2 and roughly half of that gain (+11%) in October alone. UBS cites its defensive characteristics and structural growth opportunities from AI and longevity.

sector_views.rationale: XLV +23% in H2, +11% in October, as capital rotates out of Tech. Defensive characteristics plus structural growth from AI and longevity make it a compelling destination for capital.
Elevated exposures and funding fears are pushing incremental dollars elsewhere. Retail is buying the dip in Tech ETFs and Semis/Memory stocks, and CTA selling is close to exhaustion.
